chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman who has a husband who has lost his sanity after marrying her, or insanity befalls him. He said: 'She has the right to remove herself from him if she wishes.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And if she married him while he was sane, and it became apparent to her that he was stubborn/insane, she should wait for him for one year. If he connects with her once, he has the right to keep her.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (Ima al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.عِنِّينٌ: stubborn or insane (contextually referring to persistent condition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wife if her husband becomes insane after marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *'Inan* (stubbornness/insanity) in marriage, granting the wife unilateral authority (*khiyar*) to dissolve the union if her husband's mental faculties deteriorate post-nuptially. Shaykh al-Tusi adds a crucial jurisprudential nuance: if the husband was sane at the time of marriage, the wife must observe a one-year waiting period; if he 'connects' with her during this time, the marriage bond is re-established, preventing immediate dissolution.
